title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with new partnerships and funding, while some projects continue to lag behind schedule. As the U.S. ramps up its space resilience efforts, the dual-use debate adds a layer of complexity to defense strategies.

themes.title: European Firms Join NASA Program
themes.body: NASA's inclusion of three European companies in its commercial data program signals a growing reliance on international partnerships for data acquisition. This move may bolster the agency's capabilities while also raising questions about data sovereignty.

themes.title: Defense Budget Increases
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion boost for space resilience indicates a strong commitment to enhancing U.S. capabilities in the face of evolving threats. This funding could lead to a flurry of contracts and initiatives aimed at fortifying national security.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Delays
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing reflect the challenges of developing cutting-edge defense technologies. As competitors advance, these setbacks could impact the U.S.'s strategic edge in this critical area.

themes.title: Space Domain Awareness Gains Traction
themes.body: With Slingshot's data now accessible on the .mil cloud, the military's ability to monitor space activities is set to improve significantly. This development underscores the increasing importance of space domain awareness in national defense strategies.
